subtopicTitle: Surface area and volume of all above 3D shapes

cards.front: State the fundamental formulas for the volume and total surface area of a cube with side length $s$.
What are the formulas for the volume and total surface area of a sphere with radius $r$?
cards.back:
Volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.
Total Surface Area $A = 4\pi r^2$.

cards.front: A cylindrical water tank has a radius of $2 \text{ m}$ and a height of $5 \text{ m}$. Calculate its volume and total surface area.
cards.back:
Volume $V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (2^2)(5) = 20\pi \text{ m}^3$.
Total Surface Area $A = 2\pi r h + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi (2)(5) + 2\pi (2^2) = 20\pi + 8\pi = 28\pi \text{ m}^2$.

cards.front: Explain the difference between lateral surface area and total surface area for a cone. Provide their formulas given radius $r$ and slant height $l$.
cards.back:
Lateral surface area ($A_L$) is the area of the curved surface only. Total surface area ($A_T$) includes the curved surface and the base area.
Lateral Surface Area $A_L = \pi r l$.
Total Surface Area $A_T = \pi r l + \pi r^2 = \pi r(l+r)$.

cards.front: Derive the general formula for the volume of any pyramid or cone with base area $B$ and height $h$.
cards.back:
The volume of any pyramid or cone is one-third of the product of its base area and its height. This can be intuitively understood by comparing it to a prism/cylinder with the same base and height.
$V = \frac{1}{3} \times \text{Base Area} \times \text{Height} = \frac{1}{3} B h$.

cards.front: A rectangular prism (cuboid) has dimensions $3 \text{ cm} \times 4 \text{ cm} \times 5 \text{ cm}$. If all its dimensions are doubled, how does its volume change?
cards.back:
Original volume $V_1 = 3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60 \text{ cm}^3$.
New dimensions are $6 \text{ cm} \times 8 \text{ cm} \times 10 \text{ cm}$.
New volume $V_2 = 6 \times 8 \times 10 = 480 \text{ cm}^3$.
The volume increases by a factor of $V_2/V_1 = 480/60 = 8$. (It increases by $2^3$, as all three dimensions were doubled).

cards.front: How does the volume of a cone relate to the volume of a cylinder if both have the same base radius $r$ and height $h$?
cards.back:
The volume of a cone is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height.
Cylinder Volume: $V_{cyl} = \pi r^2 h$.
Cone Volume: $V_{cone} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.
Ratio: $V_{cone} / V_{cyl} = 1/3$.

cards.front: A solid metal cuboid with dimensions $10 \text{ cm} \times 5 \text{ cm} \times 2 \text{ cm}$ is melted down and recast into a cube. What is the side length of the new cube?
cards.back:
Volume of the cuboid $V_{cuboid} = 10 \times 5 \times 2 = 100 \text{ cm}^3$.
When recast, the volume remains the same. Let $s$ be the side length of the new cube.
Volume of cube $V_{cube} = s^3$.
So, $s^3 = 100 \text{ cm}^3$.
$s = \sqrt[3]{100} \text{ cm}$.
